before: There's nothing worse than, you know, getting up there and the cape is bunching up or something like that. So then, the secret door — this is one of the shelves you don't see when you walk in, but it slowly opens.
after: It opens and then this is the tutoring center in the back. (Applause) So you can see the full effect!
ru: Вы можете видеть ее посередине рядом с крюками.

quote: They can even use this grappling hook like a sling shot and fling themselves forward.
before: Some bacteria take Batman's approach. They use grappling hooks to pull themselves along.
after: Others use chemical engineering. H. pylori lives only in the slimy, acidic mucus inside our stomachs.
ru: Они даже могут применять этот захватный «крюк» в качестве рогатки, чтобы бросить себя вперёд.

quote: Meanwhile, two hooks are pulling them apart— that’s the repulsive force expanding the universe.
before: To understand these three scenarios, imagine two objects representing galaxies. A short, tight rubber band is holding them together — that’ s the attractive force of gravity.
after: Copy this system over and over again, and you have something approximating the real universe. The outcome of the battle between these two opposing forces determines how the end of the universe will play out.
ru: Вместе с тем в противоположном направлении их тянут закреплённые крючками верёвки — это сила отталкивания, расширяющая Вселенную.

quote: Comments such as "Captain Hook" and "Hook off Hooky" have been used.
before: The defense barrister warned the jury to ignore the comments of the press as they may have convicted the defendant before the trial has begun.
after: Mr. Fitzgerald told them of "exaggeration and misrepresentation by the media".

quote: And you're still under 18, so, hopefully, they won't put you in jail.
before: I don't know anything other than you have to turn yourself in. If the cops are looking for you, you have to turn yourself in.
after: Why aren't you at school? Why aren't you at school?
ru: И, тебе ещё нет 18, так что, надеюсь, они не посадят тебя в тюрьму.

quote: We should hear something hopefully from the Kings soon.
before: JAX: Okay, good. Hap's with the Irish.
after: - How's things going here? - TIG: Fine.
ru: Надеюсь, очень скоро Короли выйдут на связь.

quote: Hopefully it's nothing, but I don't want to scare her off the wedding just yet, okay?
before: All right, just listen then. Something is going on.
after: Mm-hmm. That would be bad.
ru: Очень надеюсь, что ничего ужасного, но я не хочу просто так пугать ее прямо перед свадьбой.

quote: And hopefully we'll both find other people one day.
before: No. We're much better suited as friends.
after: Of course you will, Trixie. There.
ru: И надеюсь, однажды мы оба встретим свою пару.

quote: So, I hopefully am writing, you know, books that are good for children and for adults.
before: And what you have to do is, you really have to edit down to what you want to say. And hopefully, you're not talking down to kids and you're not talking in such a way that you, you know, couldn't stand reading it after one time.
after: But the painting reflects — I don't think differently for children than I do for adults. I try to use the same kind of imagination, the same kind of whimsy, the same kind of love of language.
ru: Так что, знаете, я надеюсь, что пишу хорошие книги и для детей, и для взрослых.

quote: And people are bringing their green industries, hopefully their green restaurants, to the Green School.
before: This was a great thing. But more than that, people are building green houses around Green School, so their kids can walk to school on the paths.
after: It's becoming a community. It's becoming a green model.
ru: Люди привозят своё экологичное производство, надеюсь, привезут и экологичные рестораны, в Зеленую Школу.

quote: I'm going to talk to you today about hopefully converting fear into hope.
after: When we go to the physician today — when we go to the doctor's office and we walk in, there are words that we just don't want to hear. There are words that we're truly afraid of.
ru: Я расскажу вам сегодня, о превращении страха в надежду.

quote: So a Grand Final at home, hopefully we can win that one.
before: "It'll be nice to send Kez off. This is her last season.
after: And give her a good send off."

quote: Didn't want to let go of his horns, huh?
before: You all right? Can-can you sit?
after: Not even if it killed him. People are strange.
ru: Не хотел расставаться с рогами?

quote: I'm assuming these are some kind of horns they bought at Comic-Con?
before: I guess this is what we get for being with two testosterone-fueled alpha males. At some point, they're bound to lock horns.
after: I'm really sorry they took Sheldon's spot away. He shouldn't have to suffer just because Howard's such a big deal now.
ru: Могу предположить, что эти рога они купили на Комик-Коне.

quote: There's blood on the horns as well as the hanging wire on the back.
before: Booth? Yeah.
after: Did you cut your little finger on the back of the wire there? Yeah, a month ago when I hung the mask.
ru: Здесь кровь на рогах как и на шнурках, висящих сзади.

quote: And I'm not one to toot my own horn, but you know what?
before: You're coming back immediately. Ma'am, I really think I can do this.
after: I'm gonna toot... and say that I just saved a lot of people. We are so close to getting Rayna and that bomb.
ru: И я не один гудок свой рог, , но вы знаете, что?

quote: How can we disengage or unhook ourselves from the horns of the amygdala?
before: (Laughter) But fear is the central underlying underpinning of all of our response systems. Fight-or-flight is one of the earliest, some say reptilian, response to our environment.
after: (Laughter) Well, I'd like to tell you the secret right now. (Applause) This is all making much, much too much sense.
ru: Как нам избежать или отцепить себя от рогов миндалины?

quote: It retains its crescent shape and moves in the direction of the horns.
before: The beautiful thing is that it moves bodily. It's what's technically known as a " barchan, " and the entire dune walks across the desert in a westerly direction at a speed of about 17 meters per year.
after: What happens is that the wind blows the sand up the shallow slope on the other side, and then, as each sand grain hits the top of the ridge, it cascades down on the inside of the crescent, and so the whole horn-shaped dune moves. Steve Grand points out that you and I are, ourselves, more like a wave than a permanent thing.
ru: Она сохраняет форму полумесяца и движется по направлению рогов.

quote: As the juveniles are growing up, their horns actually curve backwards.
before: When you have a little museum, you have little dinosaurs. (Laughter) If you look at the Triceratops, you can see it's changing, it's shape-shifting.
after: And then as they get older, the horns grow forward. And that's pretty cool.
ru: По мере того, как молодые особи росли, их рога росли назад.

quote: Witnesses report the train sounded its horns at the appropriate times.
after: It was reported the pickup truck simply drove in front of the train.

quote: Actually, I saved you from the horrible post-differential traffic jam.
before: Elaborate measures? We took a walk-- a walk you would have taken anyway.
after: Meningococcus. We believe the rash under Julie's armpit is actually petechial spots.
ru: На самом деле, я спас тебя от ужасного постдифференциального застоя.

quote: It's turning into a horrible, frightening place for old people.
before: My husband is a good man. This country is going to the dogs.
after: I've heard it all before, love. ..for vulnerable people.
ru: Для пожилых она превращается в ужасное, пугающее место.

quote: Would you still care about me if I did horrible things?
before: That's all. It's nothing to do with you.
after: Yes, of course. Absolutely.
ru: Ты бы любил меня, если бы я делал ужасные вещи?

quote: And I've learned that being afraid and hiding things is a horrible way to live.
before: But I did. I did survive it.
after: I don't want that for you. I want you to help me find Debbie's killer so I can protect you from them.
ru: И я узнала, что бояться и скрывать - это ужасный способ жить.

quote: And yet our laws tell her that she committed a horrible crime equivalent to child pornography.
before: Jennifer did nothing wrong. All she did was share a nude photo with someone she thought that she could trust.
after: Our gender norms tell her that by producing this nude image of herself, she somehow did the most horrible, shameful thing. And when we assume that privacy is impossible in digital media, we completely write off and excuse her boyfriend's bad, bad behavior.
ru: И всё же закон гласит, что она совершила ужасное преступление сродни детской порнографии.

quote: After a brief period of really horrible withdrawal feeling, like lack-of-caffeine headache, I now feel lovely.
before: So thank you. (Audio) Woman 3: Deleting the Twitter app was very sad, and I feel I maybe, over the last year when I've been on Twitter, have developed an addiction to it, and this " Bored and Brilliant " challenge has really made me realize it.
after: I had a lovely dinner with my family, and I hope to continue this structured use of these powerful tools. (Audio) Woman 4: I don't have that guilty gut feeling I have when I know I'm wasting time on my phone.
ru: После короткого действительно ужасного периода, будто голова болела от нехватки кофеина, теперь я себя чувствую прекрасно.

quote: But we rarely do that when we're having a bad day, and something horrible is happening.
before: It's not — we tend to take our cameras out when we're doing awesome things. Or we're, " Oh, yeah, this party, let me take a picture. "
after: And I found that it's actually been very, very important to record even just that one second of a really bad moment. It really helps you appreciate the good times.
ru: Но мы редко делаем подобное, когда у нас плохой день, и когда что-то ужасное происходит.

quote: La Riva described the military as a "horrible" use of the working class.
before: Carroll recalled someone who went to fight in the Vietnam War and returned changed. He wondered how the US can train people to be racist killers and then expect them to return to society.
after: She called the Korean War a "genocidal war." Pierce then explained he was an honorary ambassador in Korea.

quote: You know, the horrors that these young people endure while fighting for their country.
before: I spoke to his sister. She said he was self- medicating with alcohol.
after: Is it any wonder they're unable to cope with daily life? We have an epidemic of homeless veterans on our nation's streets.
ru: Знаете, те ужасы, которые пережили эти молодые люди, защищая свою страну.

quote: Believe me, it was a real house of horrors.
before: Yeah, it's not half as bad as Hannah said it was. No, it was.
after: Yeah. I'm surprised you live in such a nice place. No offense.
ru: Поверь мне, это был дом ужасов.

quote: Paid her to get the whole horror show on tape To get mcdonnell to resign.
before: Because he had to. Someone leaked it to the press that it was charles Who set up diaper boy.
after: And now susan ross Is going to be the next senator of virginia. You leaked it.
ru: Он подослал к нему женщину, заплатил ей, чтобы она записала это шоу ужасов, чтобы МакДоннел ушел в отставку.

quote: I never told you the reality of the horror.
before: Fairy tales aren't real. But it was just my fantasy of what this place should be.
after: Okay. All right.
ru: Я никогда не рассказывала тебе о том, что существует ужас.

quote: But this wasn't a scene from a horror film or a gruesome police report.
before: On September 1st, 1953, William Scoville used a hand crank and a cheap drill saw to bore into a young man's skull, cutting away vital pieces of his brain and sucking them out through a metal tube.
after: Dr. Scoville was one of the most renowned neurosurgeons of his time, and the young man was Henry Molaison, the famous patient known as " H.M. ", whose case provided amazing insights into how our brains work. As a boy, Henry had cracked his skull in an accident and soon began having seizures, blacking out and losing control of bodily functions.
ru: Но это не сцена из фильма ужасов или душераздирающий полицейский отчёт.

quote: I want people to see what's happening underwater, both the horror and the magic.
before: But more and more frequently these days I'm seeing terrible things underwater as well, things that I don't think most people realize. And I've been compelled to turn my camera towards these issues to tell a more complete story.
after: The first story that I did for National Geographic, where I recognized the ability to include environmental issues within a natural history coverage, was a story I proposed on harp seals. The story I wanted to do initially was just a small focus to look at the few weeks each year where these animals migrate down from the Canadian arctic to the Gulf of St. Lawrence in Canada to engage in courtship, mating and to have their pups.
ru: Я хочу, чтобы люди увидели, что на самом деле происходит в подводном мире, все: и ужасы, и великолепие.

quote: My relationship with the internet reminds me of the setup to a clichéd horror movie.
after: You know, the blissfully happy family moves in to their perfect new home, excited about their perfect future, and it's sunny outside and the birds are chirping... And then it gets dark.
ru: Мои отношения с интернетом напоминают мне засаду из полного клише фильма ужасов.

quote: He then approached a director and said, "I want you to make a pure horror movie."
before: Ultimately, he began producing film projects writers would present to him in 2004. Winch said he has produced a great deal of horror-comedy films, but grew tired of reading reviews that his films weren't horror because they had comedic elements.
after: The result was his recent film, Fall of Grace. Winch said the film has been screened at 14 film festivals and he was named Best Actor at one of those events.

quote: Is it true they lie with their horses?
before: Soon. The Dothraki never stay still for long.
after: I wouldn't ask Khal Drogo. Do you take me for a fool?
ru: Это правда, что они спят со своими лошадьми?

quote: Uh, not sure you're gonna find a horse in there, mate.
before: It showed me where Emma is. Now I have to get to her.
after: I don't need a horse. I need a portal.
ru: Вряд ли ты найдешь в этом шкафу лошадь.

quote: Now that you've got your girl's horse, don't you have a dance to get to?
before: See? Told ya.
after: Now we know why she didn't want you down here. Indeed.
ru: А теперь, когда у тебя лошадь твой девушки, не хочешь ли ты отправиться на танцы?

quote: Do you know how strong booze has to be to get a horse drunk?
before: First things first-- find an ax. Are you sure about this?
after: I c--I ca-- I can't feel my face, much less my face... I mean hands. Just do it.
ru: Знаешь, сколько нужно бухла, чтобы напоить лошадь?

quote: When trains began to shuttle people across the coutryside, many insisted they would never replace horses.
after: Less than a century later, people repeated that same prediction about cars, telephones, radio, television, and computers. Each had their own host of detractors.
ru: Когда по сельской местности начали ходить пассажирские поезда, многие утверждали, что они никогда не заменят лошадей.

quote: I see this horse with a harness, dragging the snow away.
before: I see a white building. It's snowing, a soft snow.
after: Then, one night, the scene changes. I see cats and dogs walking towards me.
ru: Я вижу лошадь в упряжке, она убирает снег.

quote: So here we are back to the horse and buggy.
before: Hurricane Sandy caused a lot of people to lose the 20th century, maybe for a couple of days, in some cases for more than a week, electricity, running water, heating, gasoline for their cars, and a charge for their iPhones. The problem we face is that all these great inventions, we have to match them in the future, and my prediction that we're not going to match them brings us down from the original two-percent growth down to 0.2, the fanciful curve that I drew you at the beginning.
after: I'd like to award an Oscar to the inventors of the 20th century, the people from Alexander Graham Bell to Thomas Edison to the Wright Brothers, I'd like to call them all up here, and they're going to call back to you. Your challenge is, can you match what we achieved?
ru: Таким образом, мы вернулись к лошадям и коляскам.

quote: Horses currently in quarantine are expected to be held for another 30 days.
before: There are 80 horses currently in quarantine at either Eastern Creek in New South Wales or at the Spotswood quarantine station in Victoria. These horses are thoroughbreds brought into Australia for the spring breeding season.

quote: They're going to have to go to the hospital.
before: I had 40 hits of Ecstasy in my pocket! Buckle up, kids.
after: This boat is awesome, babe! And we're the only passengers aboard.
ru: Их придется отправить в больницу.

quote: Could you come over to the hospital tomorrow?
before: The injury on Sergeant Whitehead's leg was, erm... I don't know what it was but it wasn't from a 9mm. He's in surgery now.
after: They'll have removed the bullet from his leg and from Klara by then. I could really do with your help.
ru: Не могли бы вы заскочить в больницу завтра?

quote: Every one of these family members was at a different hospital, Different insurance, different doctors.
before: You think your serial killer only targets people who hurt others? Liz: How else do you explain this?
after: There's nothing that ties them together. Yes, there is.
ru: У каждого из членов этих семей были разные больницы, разные страховки, разные доктора.

quote: We just have to get you to the hospital.
before: There's no reason you shouldn't be. I sealed the wound.
after: Yeah. I'll tell her.
ru: Мы должны доставить тебя в больницу.

quote: Next, he watched his wife go into labor at his hospital.
before: He said they felt like two baseballs on the sides of his head. Pain just kept accumulating in his life.
after: She heaved and pushed, clearly in anguish. Her obstetrician called out to the intern on duty to give her a few drops of ether to ease her pain.
ru: Он наблюдал за родами своей жены в больнице.

quote: So, after that screening, we bring the children to the hospital.
before: That's an extreme of micropthalmos called enophthalmos. But, every so often, we come across children who show some residual vision, and that is a very good sign that the condition might actually be treatable.
after: That's the hospital we're working with in Delhi, the Schroff Charity Eye Hospital. It has a very well-equipped pediatric ophthalmic center, which was made possible in part by a gift from the Ronald McDonald charity.
ru: После осмотра мы доставляем детей в больницу.

quote: And then this is a picture of one of the most famous hospitals in America.
before: And if you look at historical pictures of the early operating rooms, they have been on top of buildings. For example, this is the oldest operating room in the Western world, in London, where the operating room is actually on top of a church with a skylight coming in.
after: This is Mass General in Boston. And do you know where the operating room is?
ru: А это изображение одной из знаменитейших больниц Америки.

quote: The driver had claimed to be taking a patient to Jamhuriat Hospital.
before: It was here the driver detonated the explosives before police could stop him. This is according to Interior Ministry spokesman Nasrat Rahimi, who also said the nearby ministry building was the apparent target.
after: Mirwais Yasini, a member of the National Assembly, was nearby when it happened. He agreed that the Interior Ministry was the intended target, however, most of the victims were people in the busy streets, he told Reuters.

quote: I see. You're mad that I killed your blond-haired, blue-eyed host, right?
before: It's much more P.C. You can call me whatever you want when I'm gutting you.
after: That's what you get for taking over somebody's body to spy on me, but congrats. You found me, so now what?
ru: Ты сходишь с ума из-за того, что я убил твою белокурую, голубоглазую хозяйку, да?

quote: The Mark of Cain never lets its host die easy.
before: Shall we discuss terms? == sync, corrected by elderman == @elder_man
after: It's just a curse. It can be removed.
ru: Печать Каина не позволит хозяину умереть спокойно.

quote: I wanted you to be a good host.
before: I know it's not the time, but you gotta watch basketball if you're gonna try to reference it. Sergeant, this is boorish behavior.
after: You told me to make it work, and I came up with a creative solution. Diaz finished her arrest reports.
ru: Я хотел, чтобы вы были приветливым хозяином.

quote: Why did you go to the party dressed as a German gameshow host?
before: Why are you wearing that jacket? Because I was at a party in India last night, and I've hurried over here.
after: Soon, I grew weary of their abuse and set off in what, be in no doubt, is my favourite car on sale today. I will admit, there are one or two tiny little problems with the 4C.
ru: Зачем ты пошёл на вечеринку одетым как немецкий ведущий?

quote: Once the parasites get in, the hosts don't get a say.
before: These hosts won't get to survive or reproduce. They have as much control over their own fates as my car.
after: Now humans, of course, are no stranger to manipulation. We take drugs to shift the chemistries of our brains and to change our moods, and what are arguments or advertising or big ideas if not an attempt to influence someone else's mind?
ru: Как только появляется паразит, хозяин тела теряет право голоса.

quote: Others might have a difficult time transmitting to new hosts.
before: It takes more than time and genetic similarity for a host jump to be successful. Some viruses come equipped to easily infect a new host’ s cells, but are then unable to evade an immune response.
after: For example, they might make the host’ s blood contagious, but not their saliva. However, once a host jump reaches the transmission stage, the virus becomes much more dangerous.
ru: Другим сложнее мигрировать к новым хозяевам.

quote: Just because Sebastian is a wonderful host does not mean that he can assemble Ikea furniture.
before: Those guys are measuring influence, not behaviors that indicate our trustworthiness. But the most important thing that we have to keep in mind is that reputation is largely contextual.
after: The big challenge is figuring out what data makes sense to pull, because the future's going to be driven by a smart aggregation of reputation, not a single algorithm. It's only a matter of time before we'll be able to perform a Facebook- or Google-like search and see a complete picture of someone's behaviors in different contexts over time.
ru: То, что Себастьян прекрасный хозяин, не значит, что он может собрать мебель из IKEA.

quote: A Hong Kong radio host Wong Yuk Man has been sacked last week.
after: Wong hosted a radio program which had helped him become famous by criticizing the government and the pro-Beijing political party. Commercial Radio, a private radio station and Wong’s former employee said Wong was fired because he demanded a 5-days-per-week program which the station could not deliver.

quote: Can I use your hot tub whenever I want?
before: I could really use a hug. Please don't ruin this for me!
after: Yeah. Just no more man-made bubbles.
ru: А я смогу пользоваться вашей горячей ванной, когда захочу?

quote: Rhinoceros horn is cold, and only used on men, because they're hot.
before: I told Jenny it would help her back. That's not true.
after: We are. I was trying to cool her spirits.
ru: Носорожий рог холодный, и используется только мужчинами, потому что они горячие.

quote: And then I get seen by this totally hot beach bunny, and it is on!
before: It's for this sports deodorant. I play this athletic stud who spikes volleyballs and works out.
after: I want that product. Thanks for believing in me, Bobby.
ru: А потом меня замечает горячая цыпочка с пляжа, и поехали!

quote: The Hot Ness Monster is an elusive beast.
before: Are you wearing sun block? Any spottings?
after: What do you think, Mandi. Over there? Prime real estate.
ru: Горячий монстр Мыса - неуловимое животное.

quote: It was dusty and it was terribly hot.
before: I visited this camp. It's in Djibouti, neighboring Somalia, and it was so remote that we had to take a helicopter to fly there.
after: And we went to visit a school and started talking to the children, and then I saw this girl across the room who looked to me to be the same age as my own daughter, and I went up and talked to her. And I asked her the questions that grown-ups ask kids, like, " What is your favorite subject? "
ru: Там было очень пыльно и ужасно жарко.

quote: Or that time you burned the roof of your mouth on a hot slice of pizza?
before: Do you remember your first kiss?
after: What about playing tag or duck, duck, goose as a child? These are all instances where we're using touch to understand something.
ru: Или когда вы впервые обожгли себе язык о горячий кусок пиццы?

quote: Well, we know of warm little ponds. We call them "hot springs."
before: Now, in order for you to understand the significance of geyserite, I need to take you back a couple of centuries. In 1871, in a letter to his friend Joseph Hooker, Charles Darwin suggested: " What if life started in some warm little pond with all sort of chemicals still ready to undergo more complex changes? "
after: In these environments, you have hot water dissolving minerals from the underlying rocks. This solution mixes with organic compounds and results in a kind of chemical factory, which researchers have shown can manufacture simple cellular structures that are the first steps toward life.
ru: Мы называем такие водоемы горячими источниками.

quote: The organizers defended their action claiming Sydney was "a hot bed of racism."
before: Co-promoter Ken West caused a stir when the flag was "banned" from this year's Big Day Out in Sydney after organisers branded it a "gang colour" and symbol of hate. Organizers of the rock festival had planned to confiscate any flag or bandanna bearing the national symbol at the gate.
after: They had already moved the event from the traditional time, Australia Day, to avoid these "nationalistic overtones." The Prime Minister John Howard responded by declaring that the Big Day Out should have been cancelled unless organisers reversed their decision to ban the flag.

quote: Otherwise, we would have been there for hours.
before: That was just bullying! APPLAUSE
after: I can do that, literally, all day. That is not an exercise.
ru: В противном случае, мы могли так стоять часами.

quote: He's here 48 hours and you're on the phone with your sponsor.
before: It was Louise. I just wanted to talk through some things.
after: - It's not a big deal. - And what did she say?
ru: Он здесь всего 48 часов, а ты уже звонишь своему попечителю.

quote: Then within the next three to four hours, we go into a coma, sir.
before: Sergeant... how long do we have without antirad? After the first three hours, we begin to feel the first effects and the first hallucinations.
