after: I get it. Lotta flasks.
ru: Здесь есть серебряные фляжки, золотые фляжки, деревянные фляжки, фляжки с крышками, фляжки с кнопками...

quote: And I remember the smell of his wooden shield.
before: I remember my father's hands. They were rough, like sandstone, but so gentle.
after: I don't think I was supposed to play with it, but he let me anyway. And this.
ru: Еще я помню запах его деревянного щита.

quote: What good is wooden stick if the other guy's got a gun?
before: Well, how about you don't take it out on me? I don't even know why you're teaching us how to use these things.
after: You ever heard of Slade Wilson? He could take you down in about two seconds with a wooden stick.
ru: Что проку от деревянных палок, если у чувака есть ствол?

quote: We found a wooden stake with your fingerprints all over it.
before: Do you understand that? (mutters) were you in the cemetery with Crow?
after: Ah! The cat creeps in to kill the bird.
ru: Мы нашли деревянный кол с Вашими отпечатками повсюду.

quote: And the marimba, for everybody like me, it was this huge, wooden xylophone.
before: A few years later, I was at my next research job at Georgia Tech in Atlanta, and I was working in a group dealing with robotic musicians. And I thought, music: that's the perfect place to look at teamwork, coordination, timing, improvisation — and we just got this robot playing marimba.
after: And when I was looking at this, I looked at other works in human-robot improvisation — yes, there are other works in human-robot improvisation — and they were also a little bit like a chess game. The human would play, the robot analyzed what was played, and would improvise their own part.
ru: Маримбой для таких, как я, был вот этот огромный деревянный ксилофон.

quote: Some families donated their doors and wooden beds to repair roads.
before: Their catch cries were, " Everything for our Southern brothers! " and, " We will not worry about our houses if the vehicles have not yet gotten through. "
after: Vietnamese forces even used deception to get the U.S. aircraft to bomb mountainsides in order to make gravel for use in building and maintaining roads. The all-pervading red dust seeped into every nook and cranny.
ru: Некоторые семьи жертвовали двери и деревянные кровати, чтобы отремонтировать дорогу.

quote: This is a bronze ball, an aluminum arm here, and then this wooden disk.
before: This is a sculpture I made, which is a way of, kind of, freeing a form into an object that has different degrees of freedom. So, it can balance on a point.
after: And the wooden disk was really thought about as something that you'd want to hold on to, and that would glide easily through your hands. The aluminum is because it's very light.
ru: Это бронзовый шар, алюминиевая ручка здесь, и деревянный диск.

quote: Professor Mark Wooden from the Melbourne Institute said, "There is no economic sense in it."
before: The claims of the Government are highly debated and not supported by some independent expert assesment.
after: A report issued by 17 independent experts in industrial relations from Australian tertiary institutions stated that there "is no convincing evidence that the proposals will generate jobs," and that the "claim that individual contracts deliver a higher productivity is highly questionable."

quote: I wish you wouldn't use the word "vaccine."
before: Fast and efficient ... the perfect delivery mechanism. Uh, hey, um, not that it was easy to find a mineralized solution that could suspend the vaccine and conduct electricity.
after: It's really more of an antiserum. Okay, so... these antibodies should be able to target the virus' antigens, if this bloody alien virus even has antigens.
ru: Я хотела бы, чтобы ты не использовал слово "вакцина".

quote: "I'd also like to thank ASA Polmar for saying such nice words."
before: It was a joke, Eli. That's all.
after: Yes. - He's introducing you?
ru: "Я также хочу поблагодарить заместителя прокурора Полмара за такие добрые слова."

quote: Uh, Amy, it's filtering out like every other word.
before: Ma'am, if I could interrupt. I really think that...
after: Usually I just do that myself. Okay, this is why we need a steady hand like Bill Ericsson.
ru: Эми, до нас долетает только каждое второе слово.

quote: It's got the word "love" on it in every language!
before: Oh,gimme! Look at this wrapping paper.
after: I literally--i put no thought into the wrapping at all. Might as well have been toilet paper.
ru: Слово "любовь" написано на всех языках!

quote: Let me end it with words from politicians who were similarly distant.
before: And then we're off to the races, because I don't believe for a second that we have forgotten how to solve tough challenges or that we have become too apathetic or hard-hearted to even try. I started my talk with quotes from wordsmiths who were separated by an ocean and a century.
after: Winston Churchill came to my home of MIT in 1949, and he said, " If we are to bring the broad masses of the people in every land to the table of abundance, it can only be by the tireless improvement of all of our means of technical production. " Abraham Lincoln realized there was one other ingredient.
ru: Позвольте мне закончить словами политиков, которые также были далеко.

quote: And this we can say without a single word.
before: Where sameness is safeness, with something as simple as what we wear, we can draw every eye to ourselves to say that there are differences in this world, and there always will be. Get used to it.
after: Fashion can give us a language for dissent. It can give us courage.
ru: И мы можем сказать это, не произнося ни слова.

quote: The word is "pizzled": it's a combination of puzzled and pissed off.
before: And they said, well, the fundamental thing you have to do is turn off your BlackBerry, close your laptop, end your daydream and pay full attention to the person. There is a newly coined word in the English language for the moment when the person we're with whips out their BlackBerry or answers that cell phone, and all of a sudden we don't exist.
after: (Laughter) I think it's quite apt. It's our empathy, it's our tuning in which separates us from Machiavellians or sociopaths.
ru: Это слово "дивотраханный", от слов "удивлённый" и "затраханный".

quote: Part of the advertisement contained a definition of the word "exercise book".
before: On August 21, the Polish weekly Przekrój published an advertisement for Dan-Mark exercise books, bearing the logo of 4fun.tv, a Polish music/interactive TV station.
after: The wording looked familiar, and Wikinews consulted Wikipedia, the collaborative online encyclopedia.

quote: Well, there's gotta be some kind of workaround, right?
before: Somebody's bound to notice that. All right.
after: It's a technical problem. You guys are technical guys.
ru: Но ведь должен быть какой-нибудь обходной путь, верно?

quote: Well, I can't fix it from out here, unless you have some workaround for basic physics.
before: Not sure how else to say it. You can't come in here without a pass.
after: Do you? Fine.
ru: Я же не могу починить все отсюда, если только у вас нет временного решения этой проблемы.

quote: He's probably already got a workaround, you know?
before: You, uh... You realize the Master saw all this through the eyes of those munchers, right?
after: No, no, no, he didn't see shit. The signal paralyzed their communication systems when it paralyzed them.
ru: Наверняка он уже нашел обходной путь, понимаешь?

quote: If I had a day, maybe I could find a workaround, but in an hour, not so much.
before: Fitz, is there any other way to fix the transponder signal? Scrambled.
after: Then we need to break Zaikin. There's no time for anything else.
ru: Был бы у меня день, может я бы придумал обходной путь, но за час — ничего не выйдет.

quote: And Bradovich, Charney, and Talbot were the only full-time workers.
before: Is this the stuff from Visualize? Yeah, it's mostly letters from the farm to Visualize asking for more help and more money.
after: But Visualize was sending temporary people all the time-- some members, some potential recruits. Their names weren't even recorded most of the time.
ru: И Брадович, Чарни и Талбот были единственными постоянными работниками.

quote: Nicole Gordon, one of the 15 missing American aid workers has been found alive.
before: Unbelievable. Nothing has changed, has it, Em?
after: Do you really think we'd let you leave? You know too much.
ru: Николь Гордон, одна из пропавших американских гуманитарных работников была найдена живой.

quote: Only workers chose to strike and certainly you have done everything possible to help.
before: Dear Margaret, if Uncle would bring you all home you would not have witnessed so much suffering. As it considers guilty Margaret, certainly not your fault.
after: Even when I was little always doing the right thing. I noticed the color of the fruit.
ru: Рабочие сами устроили забастовку, а ты, конечно же, им помогаешь.

quote: Four transit workers were electrocuted when a subway train jumped the tracks.
before: So hurry up and get your votes in for New York's cutest doggie. ...and most of all, she was sick of all the stupid puns.
after: Stay tuned for the... shocking derails. Joel, people died.
ru: Четверых работников метро убило током, когда поезд сошел с рельс.

quote: In the face of extreme immorality, domestic workers can be our moral compass.
before: So really important progress is being made. But I would argue tonight that one of the most important things that domestic workers can provide is actually what they can teach us about humanity itself and about what it will take to create a more humane world for our children.
after: And it makes sense, because what they do is so fundamental to the very basics of human need and humanity. They are there when we are born into this world; they shape who we become in this world; and they are with us as we prepare to leave this world.
ru: Домашние работники могут быть нашим моральным компасом перед лицом крайней аморальности.

quote: We have nurses and midwives and community health workers.
before: Lawyers are crucial in that fight, no doubt, but we can't leave it to lawyers alone. In health care, for example, we don't just rely on doctors to serve patients.
after: The same should be true of justice. Community legal workers, sometimes we call them community paralegals, or barefoot lawyers, can be a bridge.
ru: У нас есть медсёстры и работники больницы.

quote: The six people in the photo are Xia Gang workers.
before: It refers to those people who lost their jobs during China's transition from a planned economy to a market economy. From 1998 to 2000, 21.37 million people lost their jobs in China.
after: I made them invisible in the deserted shop wherethey had lived and worked all their lives. On the wall behind them is the slogan of the Cultural Revolution: " The core force leading our cause forward is the Chinese Communist Party. "
ru: Шесть человек на этой фотографии — уволенные работники.

quote: They need time to organize poll workers who do not have experience.
before: According to the council they need more time to organize the election process. They say they would not be able to set up polling stations by the December 27 date set by Prime Minister Latortue a few days ago.
after: One council member said that "for practical reasons, it was inevitable that we would miss the deadline," but that they would not miss the January 8 deadline currently set. They need time to print ballots, train poll workers, and distribute voter identification cards, an effort to fight potential voter fraud.

quote: I'm not scared of the workload or the time commitment.
before: I am ready. Sir, I want this.
after: What I'm scared of is looking back on my life ten years from now and realizing I didn't challenge myself to do more with it. So I can't change your opinion of me, but I got news for you: I'm going to write this supervisor exam whether you help me or not.
ru: Я не боюсь нагрузки или сроков обязательства.

quote: I've, uh, been asked to redistribute the workload.
before: - I'm not afraid of you. Okay, listen...
after: Jessica focused too much on the flash. These cases won't make The New York Times, but they'll definitely bankroll our bonuses.
ru: Меня попросили перераспределить нагрузку.

quote: Not just the workload, but the nature of the work.
before: It's way beyond that. James, it's too much -- all that you've taken on.
after: Look around. See a lot of cops, do you?
ru: Я не просто об объёме работы говорю, а о её сути.

quote: Jim had an interesting idea to help you with this extra workload.
before: Is there anybody else could run the day-to-day of the branch? I could continue to run it myself, that's...
after: And it involved you being promoted to oversee. All Northeast sales. And then Jim would be promoted to your position.
ru: Джим предложил интересную идею помочь тебе с дополнительным объемом работы.

quote: This gives us a measure of mental workload, how much the driver is actually challenged cognitively at any point along the track.
before: In contrast, theta waves are associated with a lot of cognitive activity, like visual processing, things where the driver is thinking quite a bit. Now, we can measure this, and we can look at the relative power between the theta waves and the alpha waves.
after: Now, we wanted to see if we could actually record this on the track, so we headed down south to Laguna Seca. Laguna Seca is a legendary raceway about halfway between Salinas and Monterey.
ru: Это позволит нам оценить нагрузку на мозг, понять, насколько гонщик использует когнитивные функции мозга в любой точке гоночной трассы.

quote: Contador and Rasmussen had an animated discussion about how to share the workload up the final climb.
after: Contador was happy to sit behind the yellow jersey-wearing Rasmussen, and pass him in the final sprint for the finish-line. The Dane had hoped for more help in setting the pace and extending his overall lead.

quote: I get that I am not the best in the world.
before: Well, they're European. Of course they're going to be better.
after: I have even come to terms with not being the best in America. Oh, good.
ru: Я знаю, что я не лучший в мире.

quote: Is there anything in the Fae world that can get that new doggy smell off tights?
before: I was timing that entire dumb story to see how long it would take you to realize that I actually didn't care what you were talking about, but now, even that's boring. Hey!
after: What brings you down, Little Momma? I was helping my cuz with his pit bulls at the doggie dentist--
ru: Есть что-нибудь в мире Фейри что может убрать этот собачий запах с колготок?

quote: But how would you like to work for the most powerful company in the world?
before: A man needs to make his own way in this life. No handouts.
after: How do you mean? I need you to find someone.
ru: Но как ты смотришь на работу в самой влиятельной компании в мире?

quote: Once every few generations, the world is truly transformed.
before: Well, I guess we're free to talk, then. Change is coming, Alex.
after: The new guard takes office, and the old guard swings from the gallows. Our generation will not be spared that change.
ru: Раз в несколько поколений мир полностью изменяется.

quote: Does it make sense to participate in the existing world order?
before: What kind of world do we want? This is a fundamental question that most of us are asking.
after: We want a world where life is preserved and the quality of life is enriched for everybody, not only for the privileged. In January I saw an exhibit of Fernando Botero's paintings at the UC Berkeley library.
ru: Есть ли смысл принимать текущий порядок вещей в мире?

quote: Secondly, the world would be a better place if audiences recognized that storytelling is intellectual work.
before: So a few concluding thoughts on what audiences can do to make the world a better place. So firstly, the world would be a better place, I think, if audiences were more curious and more skeptical and asked more questions about the social context that created those stories that they love so much.
after: And I think it would be important for audiences to demand more buttons on their favorite websites, buttons for example that say, " If you liked this story, click here to support a cause your storyteller believes in. " Or " click here to contribute to your storyteller's next big idea. "
ru: Во-вторых, мир был бы лучше, если бы люди признали повествование интеллектуальной работой.

quote: The average number of children in the world is like in Colombia -- it's 2.4 today.
before: So what it is, is these four: Children should survive, children shouldn't be needed for work, women should get education and join the labor force and family planning should be accessible. Now look again at this.
after: There are countries up here which are very poor. And that's where family planning, better child survival is needed.
ru: Сегодня среднее количество детей на одну женщину в Колумбии и в мире — 2,4.

quote: England defeated Slovenia 1–0 and qualified for the World Cup too.
before: On the same day, defending world champions Germany defeated Northern Ireland 3–1 in Belfast and qualified for the World Cup with nine victories in nine qualification matches.
after: On Friday, Spain defeated Albania 3–0 and joined Germany and England to qualify.

quote: The discovery lowered the price of eggs worldwide overnight.
before: No, we do know. It's highly paid.
after: That's how important it was. The Zen-Nippon Chick Sexing School was founded.
ru: Это открытие за ночь обесценило яйца во всем мире.

quote: The obedience experiments are cited and discussed in nearly every introductory psychology textbook worldwide.
before: Our children live with their children near Boston and Toronto. Sasha never remarried.
after: My obedience film is screened for every incoming class at Westpoint. And my methods and results continue to be challenged, scorned, debunked, yet every time a new outrage is unleashed out into the world, sanctioned and systematic acts of violence, the obedience experiments re-enter the conversation, reframing unanswerable questions.
ru: Эксперимент с подчинением вспоминают и изучают почти в каждом учебнике по психологии во всём мире.

quote: Ilaria's planning to release a new version of Narvik worldwide.
before: Things are different now. Listen, Alan.
after: When? Two days, unless I can give them a viable alternative.
ru: "Илария" планирует выпустить во всем мире новую версию Нарвика.

quote: A select group of central banks are lobbying for the same legislation to be passed worldwide.
before: We're gonna create, I fear, another such system that people who are... are... are... have a... a... an inclination to react dishonestly to systems are gonna actually have a... a new opportunity. Is that not a problem?
after: Once the so called green economy laws are in place, only global mega-corporations and their subsidiaries will be allowed to do business. Van Jones, Barack Obama's first Green Job Czar, has stated repeatedly on the record that the new green economy is only a cover for a complete revolution against capitalism and the total redistribution of wealth.
ru: Избранная группа центральных банков лоббирует принятие такого же законодательства во всем мире.

quote: It's the leading disability worldwide, and people die of it every day.
before: And I went out and I interviewed person after person who was suffering with depression. One of the first people I interviewed described depression as a slower way of being dead, and that was a good thing for me to hear early on because it reminded me that that slow way of being dead can lead to actual deadness, that this is a serious business.
after: One of the people I talked to when I was trying to understand this was a beloved friend who I had known for many years, and who had had a psychotic episode in her freshman year of college, and then plummeted into a horrific depression. She had bipolar illness, or manic depression, as it was then known.
ru: Это главная причина беспомощности во всём мире, и люди умирают от этого каждый день.

quote: And the pie chart was labeled, "Causes of death in children under five worldwide."
before: In too many cases, we simply don't know. Now, I remember recently seeing an updated pie chart.
after: And there was a pretty big section of that pie chart, about 40 percent — 40 percent was labeled " neonatal. " Now, " neonatal " is not a cause of death.
ru: Диаграмма была озаглавлена так: «Причины смертности детей младше пяти лет во всём мире».

quote: The only abrupt worldwide change would have been major asteroid impacts or volcanic super-eruptions.
before: What would they have seen? Over nearly all that immense time, Earth's appearance would have changed very gradually.
after: Apart from those brief traumas, nothing happens suddenly. The continental landmasses drifted around.
ru: Единственные резкие изменения во всем мире могли бы быть вызваны серьезным воздействием астероида или вулканического супер-извержения.

quote: TB also kills more women worldwide than any other disease.
before: It is reported that the CIDA minister will increase aid to Africa twofold where TB is killing those suffering from AIDS, more than any other illness.
after: In 2006, over 9,000,000 people worldwide were infected with TB.

quote: And, honestly, if it keeps Emily from being messed with, maybe it was worth it.
before: And you got yourself into trouble instead. Well, that wasn't the plan.
after: What does Emily have to do with this? Paige might not be a one-girl kind of girl.
ru: И если честно, если это убережет Эмили от неприятностей, то оно того стоило.

quote: Only took two whole days, but you're worth it.
before: This is amazing. Just a little something I threw together.
after: Thank you. I felt bad about us not being together on Valentine's Day, but since, uh,
ru: Заняло всего лишь целых два дня, но ты того стоишь.

quote: Sometimes it takes a few tries, but it's worth it.
before: I don't have any children. Don't give up.
after: To be honest, I didn't feel. Like a real woman until I became a mother. It's a true honor.
ru: Иногда на это нужно несколько попыток, но оно того стоит.

quote: Yeah, well, whatever happens, it'll be worth it to have Jessica back.
before: What about you? Best case scenario, you get kicked off the team.
after: Are you okay? What do you need me to do?
ru: "то бы ни случилось, вернуть ƒжессику стоит того.

quote: It took about a year for me to learn this, but it's really been worth it.
before: Sit down to regular meals without distractions. Think about how your body feels when you start to eat and when you stop, and let your hunger decide when you should be done.
after: I am so much more relaxed around food than I have ever been in my life. I often don't think about it.
ru: Мне потребовался где-то год, для того чтобы привыкнуть к этим правилам, но это на самом деле стоит того.

quote: But that battle for your soul, for your authentic self, it's worth it, isn't it?
before: But every word we write in the narrative of our own lives, we come closer to uncovering what's beneath our own masks, maybe even embracing that true misfit, that true crazy one within. Oh, it'll be a fight, that's for sure.
after: It's bold; it's brave. In fact, I would say it's heroic.
ru: Сражение за вашу душу, за вашу сущность, это стоит того, не правда ли?

quote: But was it worth it? Yes, absolutely it was.
before: Audience: Encore! (Laughter) LP: I'd just like to end off by just saying this: It took me four months again to feel my hands.
after: There are very, very few people who don't know now about what is happening in the Arctic. And people ask me, " Lewis, what can we do about climate change? "
ru: Стоило ли оно того? Совершенно точно, стоило.

quote: Single puncture wound to the back of the neck.
before: If it bleeds, it leads. Looks like there's only the 1 injury.
after: The shape suggests a knife. Killer was either lucky or good.
ru: Одна колотая рана в задней части шеи.

quote: The wound is shallow, so the blade was probably small.
before: Spectacle. Yeah, but the kill itself was pretty simple-- a single slice to the carotid artery with a thin, sharp blade.
after: Like a box cutter? Follow me.
ru: Рана неглубокая,следовательно лезвие могло быть небольшим.

quote: Yeah, that's why you're walking around with the wounds of Christ.
before: Three weeks in, they were dead. I'm fine.
after: Go home. - Get six good hours.
ru: Потому ты и слоняешься тут с христовыми ранами.

quote: She was found with a lump on her head and 39 stab wounds.
before: I think you should see this. Emma Jones. August 7.
after: Spot on, sir. Did she identify her attacker?
ru: Она была найдена с шишкой на голове и 39 колотыми ранами.

quote: Can the wound or scar heal without it?
before: Everybody in the whole world knowin' about it. I'm hurt and broke down and be flowin' about it, goin' about it wrong' cause I didn't allow it.
after: Can't the way that you feel be concealed about it? Everybody has their own ideal about it, dream about it, appeal about it.
ru: Может ли рана или шрам затянуться без этого?

quote: We've even started seeing its use in wound care management with nurses and in outpatient management.
before: Now, patients can access care at a local level. This reduces their travel time, improves their access, and saves money.
after: Most recently, and quite exciting, it was used in supporting a surgeon through a cancer removal of a kidney. And I'd like to just share with you a very quick video here.
ru: Мы даже заметили, что этим пользуются медсёстры в вопросах по уходу за ранами, включая амбулаторный.

quote: We love our opponents when we tend the wound in them.
before: It cuts them off from their own capacity to love. This was my second lesson in revolutionary love.
after: Tending to the wound is not healing them — only they can do that. Just tending to it allows us to see our opponents: the terrorist, the fanatic, the demagogue.
ru: Мы любим наших противников, когда заботимся об их ранах.

quote: Snyder died from the multiple gunshot wounds on the floor of the Capitol office building.
after: The Capitol went on a full lockdown with employees, tour groups and visitors in the building at the time ordered to stay where they were.

quote: You have an unfair advantage, Miss Published Writer.
before: I haven't written a thing. You always say that and then you give the best one.
after: But, tonight you've got competition. Your signature rhyming ode?
ru: У тебя явное преимущество, "девушка-издаваемый писатель".

quote: Note to God, in my next life, I do not wanna represent writers.
before: Do you have to put it that way? In the past tense is how I put it.
after: Good luck with that. Here.
ru: Заметка для Бога, в своей следующей жизни я не хочу быть представителем писателей.

quote: Well, I mean, a lot of writers write about what they know.
before: It's about a man with two families. A wife and two daughters in Rhode Island and a mistress and bastard daughter in south Carolina.
after: If anything, it just sounds like your dad wasn't that creative this time. You know? He didn't bother to change the details that much.
ru: Ну, многие писатели пишут из личного опыта.

quote: I mean, he was such a great writer.
before: Yeah. I can't figure out what happened to the poor guy.
after: Let me let you in on a little secret, young lady... You are much more talented than you think you are.
ru: Он же был отличным писателем.

quote: I'm a writer. I imagine. I make stuff up for a living.
before: But it's also had a stunning side effect, and it wasn't until recently that I fully understood it, that I understood that saying yes to playing with my children likely saved my career. See, I have what most people would call a dream job.
after: Dream job. No.
ru: Я писатель. Я выдумываю. Я зарабатываю выдумками.

before: Coke Zero, which was first sold in 2005 in the United States, was launched in Venezuela in April and Coca-Cola Femsa, the Mexican company who bottles the drink, hoped to increase the market share for low calorie drinks by up to 200 percent.
